audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4, 5 and 6 of the level chart disagreed with both the packet chart and the page's own prose: win[4] said Sett while whys[4] says 'At 6 it's even'; win[5] said Skill while whys[5] says he out-trades your single-item profile; win[6] said Skill while whys[6] says 'he has no scaling answer'.
audit.why: Sett is an early bully (Knuckle Down max-health punches, Haymaker true damage) who falls off into stacked resists; K'Sante's two-item front-line profile is the reclaim point.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = Skill (5/10), First item = Sett (4/10), 2+ items = K'Sante (6/10), flipped in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Lvl 1-2 (his grit bully), Lvl 3, Lvl 6, 2+ items are correct timings for this lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent, and one was invented. Absent: The Show Stopper grounds — it shuts off Path Maker (W), Footwork (E) and the All Out dash; and Haymaker's shield absorbs your burst window. Invented: Sett's R was called a 'suppress-slam' four times — Riot's text says he carries and slams the target, with no suppression stated. K'Sante's R was also described as having a 'recast', which is not in Riot's text.
audit.why: Grounding is the reason a caught K'Sante cannot dash out of the slam's follow-up, and it is what actually makes his level 6 dangerous — not a suppression. The Haymaker shield is why an uncommitted burst is wasted: force the shield out first.
audit.corrected: Grounding and the Haymaker shield written into spikes[1], spikes[2], whys[4] and mid; every 'suppress' and 'recast' claim removed.
sources: kit file: sett R flags grounding

audit.why: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 and Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 — long enough that a baited one is a genuine commit window.
Riot's Path Maker text says only 'taking reduced damage' during the charge. Unstoppable status is not in the kit file and the file's empty needsResearch means unknown, not confirmed.
audit.corrected: Reworded to the damage reduction that Riot's text does state.

edits.before: Sett's passive double-punch and W store-and-smash out-trade you at Level 1 when you have only Q and no engage threat.
edits.after: Knuckle Down's max-health punches and Haymaker's stored true damage out-trade you at 1, when you have only Q and no engage.

edits.before: Even with your full Q3 knock-up at 3, his E grab-stun into a charged W wins the straight stat-check trade.
edits.after: Even with your full Q3 pull at 3, Facebreaker (16s) into a charged Haymaker wins the stat-check trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip — your W unstoppable can refuse his all-in, but mistime it and his combo still kills you.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a coinflip — W's charge soaks his stored Haymaker, but mistime it and his combo still kills you.

edits.before: At 6 it's even: your All Out gives a 1v1 but strips your bulk exactly when his R suppress-slam guarantees lockdown.
edits.after: At 6 it's even: All Out gives a 1v1 but strips your bulk when The Show Stopper grounds you and kills your dashes.

edits.before: By 2+ items you survive his W and R, out-sustain his trades, and peel with E and R recast — he has no scaling answer.
edits.after: By 2+ items you survive Haymaker and his R, out-sustain his trades, and peel with Footwork and your wall-knockback.

edits.before: Your full Q-W comes up but Sett's E grab-stun + W still wins the straight stat-check trade — respect his all-in until your bulk and Q3 lockdown can actually punish a whiff.
edits.after: Your full Q-W comes up but Facebreaker into a charged Haymaker still wins the stat-check — and his W shield eats whatever burst you answer with, so bait it out before you commit Q3.

edits.before: Sett's R suppress-slam vs your All Out: it's a coinflip on who commits first — your W unstoppable can eat his R's setup, but a clean E-grab into R still kills you if you mistime W.
edits.after: The Show Stopper vs your All Out: a coinflip on who commits first — his R grounds you, so Path Maker, Footwork and the All Out dash are all shut off if he lands it before you charge W.

edits.before: This is your window: with tank items stacked you survive his stored W true damage and R, then peel/disengage with E and recast R — Sett's grit trades fall off and you out-last him.
edits.after: This is your window: with tank items stacked you survive his stored Haymaker and R, then peel with Footwork and the R wall-knockback — Sett's grit trades fall off and you out-last him.

edits.before: Sett owns the first three levels outright — his passive double-punch and his W, which stores the damage you deal him and fires it back as a true-damage smash, beat your Q-W combo before it's even online at Level 3. Don't feed his W by trading into it; last-hit at the edge of your Q cleave and accept some chip. The trap is his E grab-stun: if he yanks you in while his W is charged, you eat the smash with no answer until your own W unstoppable comes up. Just farm and survive — this lane is about reaching your items, not winning the slap-fight.
edits.after: Sett owns the first three levels outright — his passive double-punch and his W, which stores the damage you deal him and fires it back as a true-damage smash plus a shield, beat your Q-W combo before it's even online at Level 3. Don't feed his W by trading into it; last-hit at the edge of your Q cleave and accept some chip. The trap is Facebreaker: if he yanks you in while his W is charged, you eat the smash with no answer until your own W charge is back up. Just farm and survive — this lane is about reaching your items, not the slap-fight.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 even out into a skill matchup. Your W Path Maker is the key: charge it to become unstoppable and you can refuse his E-grab into R suppress chain, then knock him back and Q3 to lock him. But mistime it and his combo still kills you, so the trade is a read on who commits first. At 6 your All Out gives you a real 1v1, but it strips your tankiness right when Sett's R is a guaranteed lockdown — don't ult into a fresh E-W unless you've already baited his stored damage empty.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 even out into a skill matchup. Your W Path Maker is the key: the charge takes reduced damage, so it soaks his Facebreaker into Haymaker, and you knock him back and Q3 to lock him. But mistime it and his combo still kills you, so the trade is a read on who commits first. At 6 your All Out gives you a real 1v1, but The Show Stopper grounds you — W, E and the All Out dash all go dead — so don't ult into a fresh E-W with his Grit full.

edits.before: This is where you reclaim the lane. By 2+ tank items his stored W smash and R suppress stop one-shotting you, and your sustained tank DPS plus E disengage and R recast let you out-last every grit trade he picks. Sett has no scaling answer to a healthy tank — he's an early-game bully whose true damage and all-in lose value the bulkier you get. Drag the game past your second item, then win teamfights by W-ing onto his carry or peeling yours out with All Out recast.
edits.after: This is where you reclaim the lane. By 2+ tank items his stored Haymaker and his slam stop one-shotting you, and your sustained tank DPS plus the Footwork disengage let you out-last every grit trade he picks. Sett has no scaling answer to a healthy tank — he's an early-game bully whose true damage and all-in lose value the bulkier you get. Drag the game past your second item, then win teamfights by W-ing onto his carry or launching him off yours.

edits.before: Use W's unstoppable charge to eat his E-grab or R setup instead of getting chain-CC'd
edits.after: Use W's damage-reduced charge to soak his Facebreaker into Haymaker instead of eating it raw

edits.before: All-in at 6 with R suppress-slam while his trades still out-stat your tank profile
edits.after: All-in at 6 with The Show Stopper, grounding you so none of your three dashes work
